title: HCF & LCM
examples: When should two flashing lights flash together again?
What is the biggest number that divides both 36 and 48?
How do I use prime factor trees for HCF?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the highest common factor and the lowest common multiple. These are useful for finding common ground between numbers.
First we will look at prime factor trees. This helps us break down any number into its basic prime building blocks. For example, let us find the prime factors of 36.
We break 36 down into two numbers, six and six. Then we break six down into two and three. So 36 is two times two times three times three. This is the prime factorisation.
To find the Highest Common Factor, we take the smallest power of each shared prime factor. For 36 and 60, we share two and three. So the HCF is two times three, which is six.
To find the Lowest Common Multiple, we take the largest power of every prime factor present. For 36 and 60, we take two squared, three squared, and five. This gives us 4 x 9 x 5, which is 180.

draw.text: LCM: Largest powers of all primes

faq.q: What is the difference between HCF and LCM?
faq.a: The HCF is the largest number that divides exactly into two or more numbers. The LCM is the smallest number that two or more numbers can divide into.

faq.q: Can I use the Venn diagram method for this?
faq.a: Yes, the Venn method is great for finding the HCF when you are dealing with a small number of numbers. It helps you see the common factors clearly.

faq.q: When should I use prime factor trees?
faq.a: You should use prime factor trees when you need to find the prime factors of a number, especially if the number is quite large.
asks: Is prime factor tree always the best way?

faq.q: Do I need to use index form for LCM?
faq.a: It is very helpful to use index form when finding the LCM. It makes it easy to see the highest power of each prime factor.

facts: Prime numbers are only divisible by one and themselves.
The prime factorisation of a number shows its prime building blocks.
The HCF must always be less than or equal to the smallest number.
The LCM must always be greater than or equal to the largest number.

quiz.say: Find the HCF of 24 and 36 using prime factors.
quiz.why: The shared prime factors are two and three, and the lowest power is two times three.

wrong.1: This uses too many factors and is not the greatest common factor.
wrong.2: This is correct, but the question asks for the fully expanded form.
wrong.3: This repeats factors unnecessarily and is not the simplest form.

quiz.say: What is the LCM of 10 and 15?
quiz.why: We take the highest power of every prime factor: two from ten, three from fifteen, and five from ten.

wrong.0: This misses the factor of two entirely.
wrong.1: This includes an extra factor of five that is not needed for the lowest common multiple.
wrong.3: This only includes the smallest factors and misses the largest required power.

quiz.say: If 40 is written as $2^3 \times 5$ and 60 as $2^2 \times 3 \times 5$, what is their LCM?
quiz.why: For LCM, we take the highest power of every prime factor present, which is two to the power of three, three to the power of one, and five to the power of one.

wrong.0: This only uses the lowest power of two, making the result too small.
wrong.1: This uses three squared, but the number 60 only has one factor of three.
wrong.2: This forgets to include the prime factor three altogether.
